caption:
Wow!! What an amazing experience!! Thank you @geescottjr and @onedotchurch for setting this up for my teammates and I!!

My relationship with the Lord has been a little hit or miss and I keep coming back to the “why” for things I have experienced. Knowing now, God has a plan and reason for everything and it’s important to put all your trust into him. From showing up to Bible study or having long conversations with teammates, my journey into learning about and having that connection with Jesus has just begun. A verse that stuck with me from the scripture:

“So we don’t look at the troubles we can see now; rather, we fix our gaze on things that cannot be seen. For the things we see now will soon be gone, but the things we cannot see will last forever.”
‭‭
2 Corinthians‬ ‭4‬:‭18‬ ‭

caption:
Transfer long snapper Collin Johnson just won a National Championship with Ohio State and is looking for a new home! He made the trip to Eau Claire Wisconsin to chase perfection and make sure he’s on top of his game so his new school gets the best snapper possible.

Collin and I noticed in his warm ups that he had an issue with how deliberate he was with his throw. It seemed that he would let go of the ball and THEN finish his hands, causing the ball to have a subtle variance to the flight.

We really drilled in what it needs to feel like to be intentional with the punch and were able to see a big difference! We also focused on his sequencing to allow him to have even more control of his body through the throw.

Looking forward to continuing to help Collin improve and find a new home!

caption:
Friday, I returned home from my final hospital stay, 9 days following my final 7 hour surgery

Here is my reality of the past 4 months:

5 separate hospital admissions
3 of them due to complications in my recovery
4 surgeries
3 times nearly dead
4 months living with a colostomy bag
2 months spent living in the hospital 
1 month spent without eating solid food or food at all
37 staples in my abdomen that had to be reopened for my 4th surgery 
2 fractured vertebrae 
Still no feeling on outside of both legs
Lost my voice for 6 weeks due to vocal cord paralysis 
30 pounds lost 
4 laxatives a day and a complete rebuild of my diet or else I would get obstructions in my intestine and would have to go back to hospital
Too many scans, tests and X-Rays to remember

Countless hours spent in the rehab room 
Countless hours spent in the gym
Countless people supporting my family and I 
1 God who performed many miracles 

Still a long recovery ahead, but see you all August 28th at Jesse Owens Memorial Stadium

caption:
1 bullet
3 surgeries, with 1 taking 10 hours 
3 weeks in hospital with most in ICU 
2 fractured vertebrae 
30 pounds lost

Almost died from the gunshot
Almost died on the operating table
Almost died from a post surgery GI bleed
I shouldn’t be here anymore but God remained faithful

Doctors said I would have to feed through a tube for the rest of my life 
Doctors said I would have an ostomy bag for the rest of my life
God had other plans

On Dec. 24 I was discharged from hospital
Yesterday I returned home

Thank you to all the Doctors, nurses and medical staff who worked on my case and gave me a 2nd chance at life 
Thank you to everyone for their thoughts and prayers
Thank you to all my family and friends who stayed with me in the hospital during the most difficult time in my life 
Thank you God for performing multiple miracles when the odds were heavily stacked against me

caption:
After 8 years it’s now time to say goodbye to my boyhood club. During these years I’ve experienced things that 12 year old me could have only hoped for. I was once a kid in the stands that used to watch Newcastle United every other week and dreamed of being able to put on that black and white shirt. I have been able to represent this unbelievable club from academy level to the 1st team and to make my Premier league debut at St James Park is something that I will never forget. I would like to give a massive thank you to all my teammates, the coaches, and the staff members who have helped me along this journey and have made it possible. 

Also I would like to thank all the NUFC fans that have shown me support throughout my time at the club. “I loved representing the city and people that are me.” I will be forever grateful for the support I have received and they will always have a place in my heart.

I will never ever forget my time here. All the ups and the downs will stay with me forever. I am just so grateful that I have been given the opportunity to play for the club that I have always supported and loved. Thanks for everything! 🤍🖤 #NUFC

caption:
Time to say goodbye to collegiate shooting. 
These years have been filled with growth, unforgettable moments, and incredible people. Time truly flies when you’re having fun, and I can definitely say that’s been the case. Never would I have imagined how much I’d gain from collegiate shooting.
Being a student-athlete has been one of the most rewarding experiences of my life. I couldn’t have asked for a better way to close this chapter with a team that became family, strangers who became friends, coaches, and mentors, and a sport I’ve only grown to love more over time. Three national championships and countless memories later, I’m walking away with a full heart. I’m endlessly grateful for everyone who’s been part of this journey over the years. Special thanks to Coach Emil Milev and Coach Anthony Lutz for making it all possible!
Shooting has always been a huge part of my life, and it never disappoints me with what it teaches and gives back. Can’t wait to see what it has in store for me next! 🎯❤️

caption:
This post has been a long time coming… 

I realized I never posted something about Olympic qualifiers because I never knew how I felt. I let the result define me and because of that I lost my identity. However I came to the conclusion during this thanksgiving season, that even though the result wasn’t what we wanted I am thankful for the journey. The support from my family and the memories made with my team are irreplaceable. I am thankful for the places and opportunities that swimming has led me to, the people I’ve met and the lessons I’ve learned. As a new chapter starts, I am extremely grateful to be able to swim at Ohio State and for the family I have there. I’m excited to see where this journey takes me. Happy thanksgiving ❤️

caption:
One year ago today we became Olympic Silver Medalists and became the first USA Artistic Swimming team to compete at the Olympic Games in 16 years. It’s pretty crazy how fast time flies from a moment you worked your entire athletic career for. The Games was so important and yet only the end of that journey, when there were so many events and hours that came before. The countless time training in the pool, emotional rollercoasters and struggles, extra effort always being put in, and the amount of conversations with my best friends I would have that made each day so worth it. The bond our team of 12 had along with our amazing coaches and staff up until the very end is what made all our dreams come true. That medal is a symbol of every ounce of effort we all put in to make that possible. I know it is what keeps pushing all of us to be the best versions of ourselves everyday, wherever our journeys may take us. I love and miss you all, happy one year ❤️ 

#olympics #paris2024 #1year #artisticswimming #usa #athletes

caption:
I always take quick videos of special experiences so I can go back and remember the little things. In honor of Olympic Day, I thought I would share just a few :)
1. Opening ceremony on boat when the Eiffel Tower started sparkling 
2. More opening ceremony ft. LeBron 
3. I decided to give away my rain poncho…we were drenched but it added to the moment 
4. Lightning storm one night with view of Olympic village (jack and I were scared)
5. Someone took Megu’s shoes by accident so Dani helped her out on the way back to the rooms 
6. We had a chaotic practice/day so Dani manifested a calm “boring”day 
7. We found out our basemark was overturned 
8. Ceremony of champions where medalists got to walk and take pics with people (fun fact I dropped someone’s phone :/)
9. Being on the today show and me practicing my French at the end 
10. Keana locked in on the way to our final swim
11. Anita being weird on our way to the cold tub 
12. Sha’carri Richardson’s USA Nails
13. Nap time during the wait to get on Opening Ceremony boats

caption:
Thank you sophomore season, you were a good one 🤍

This year was one to remember, I set out new goals with a new mindset on season and I’m so proud of myself for how much I’ve accomplished and grown as both a gymnast and a person so far. I had my collegiate debut for two events, was consistently in lineups, and just continued to work hard and pour my heart out into every single practice and competition. Although I’m devastated that my season is ending so soon, I know God’s got much bigger plans for next year and I’m ready to take on this next challenge with so much grit and determination. Thank you to my family, teammates, coaches & staff, and friends for surrounding me with so much love and support, I appreciate y’all more than you know. I truly have THE best community of people who have my back, thank you God!! Get ready to see me back out there next year better than ever ❤️ #comebackszn

caption:
“I’ve never trusted my body as much as I did this year!” - Tory Vetter said this to me in a session the other day!  So great to hear… and that trust in her body showed in her gymnastics this year (B1G 10 beam champ is pretty good I guess 😉). 

I’m so proud of how much work Tory has put in over the past 2 years.  She has struggled with shoulder instability, resulting in surgery her freshman year… so it’s awesome to see how strong and stable she is looking.  It’s hard as a college athlete (any athlete … but especially college) to want to put in extra work on top of an already busy schedule. She has a great team around her already- a fantastic trainer, strength coach, & coaching staff- adding in just a little extra helped her body feel & perform its best! 

Excited to keep progressing 🩷

If you want to chat about getting your gymnast healthier, comment HGA below & I will reach out!

caption:
Finally done with this B.S. in Biology and a Minor in African and African American Studies!!!❤️🌰🎓

I want to thank The Ohio State University for making the last two years of not only my academic career but also my athletic career so incredibly special. To my teammates and coaches: thank you for giving me the chance to be part of this team. I know I was only here for a short time, but the impact you’ve had on my life will last forever. You opened my eyes to so many things, including myself, and helped me grow into the leader I am today.

Who would’ve thought that a girl from Ann Arbor, a die-hard Team Up North fan, would become a Buckeye who now bleeds scarlet and gray?

A special shoutout to my mother: you’ve been with me from the beginning all the way through to my last assignment. You’ve always been the first person I called, from the smallest achievements to the biggest crises. You are my biggest inspiration and the rock I’ll always lean on.

To the rest of my family, thank you for being so proud, supportive, and loving. I’m forever grateful for the village I have back home.

If you’ve made it this far into the post, I want to share a bit of advice that helped get me here: Don’t be afraid of change. Even if it’s scary. Even if the original plan doesn’t work. Even if people tell you it’s not worth it. Do it anyway.

If I hadn’t taken a chance on Gym America, I wouldn’t have become a Division I athlete.
If I hadn’t entered the transfer portal, I wouldn’t have accomplished my dreams.
If I hadn’t gotten surgery before my final season, I wouldn’t have finished my 20-year gymnastics career pain-free and at my strongest.

Have fun. Life is short and moves fast. Savor every moment with the people you love.
And to quote my favorite movie: “Life is like a box of chocolates. You never know what you’re gonna get.”

With that, Sidvicious is officially an alum of The Ohio State University.

Go Bucks! ❤️🌰🎓

only you, Jesus.

only you could get thousands of students together in one arena for one name. only you could provide the way you did to make this all happen. only you would choose to use broken vessels like us. only you would exceed every prayer abundantly and more.

only you, Jesus. 

There is nothing (nothing) we can or can’t do to stop what He wants to do through and with His people. This all goes far beyond February 18th on Ohio State’s campus, but to be able to witness so closely the amount of students that gave their “Yes” to Jesus on that night was nothing short of a gift. To the generational prayers that went into all of this and for allowing us to be a small part of it. thank you.

To my 6 new best friends and “team”. This season was so fun with yall and I wouldn’t trade a thing to have it any other way with anyone else. The Lord knew I needed you guys. I am so proud of each of you individually and could not be more excited to see how the Lord continues to use each of your gifts. I look up to you guys more than you know & thank God everyday for blessing me with friends that show me Jesus in the way you lead and love everyone around you.  I love how intentional Jesus is.

this is just the beginning. 
“Look at the nations and watch— and be utterly amazed. For I am going to do something in your days that you would not believe, even if you were told.”
‭‭Habakkuk‬ ‭1‬:‭5‬

What I got to experience alongside these girls (and Pat) in the last few months is something I will forever be grateful for. It’s no coincidence our motto this year ended up as “Believe It.” 
“Blessed is she who has believed that the Lord would fulfill what he has spoken to her!” Luke‬ ‭1‬:‭4‭5

athlete.bio: Hailing from a small Ohio town, this fierce competitor combines relentless determination with a strategic mind. Known for exceptional teamwork and unyielding spirit, she leaves her mark on every game.

caption:
Conventions were a huge part of my life growing up. I met some of my best friends and had the absolute best times 🥹 And now, I get incredible opportunity to teach at one. If only little me could see this dream come true. I’m endlessly thankful for my family, my mentors, and everyone who poured into me along the way. Their love and guidance made this possible, and I can’t wait to pour that same light and inspiration into the next generation 💫

It has and always will be important to me to honor where I came from and the people who shaped me. My family will forever be my first and greatest mentors, they are the reason I am the dancer and person I am today. Getting to do it all alongside my sister makes it even more special. Sharing this dream with someone who’s been there from the start is truly indescribable 🤍

These past few days have been so emotional, realizing I get to call this my job. It’s a full-circle and unforgettable moment. Also, it’s a huge reminder to always stay humble, grateful, and committed to lifting others up along the way. Never forget where you came from, and never stop giving back to those that helped shape and always supported you 🌟

Cannot wait to dance with everyone this season! Here we go season 1 of @pressplay 🤩🥳

caption:
Since graduating, my relationship with dance has looked really different. For so long, dance has been tied to goals, performance, and being on the floor every day. Stepping away from that routine has been harder than I expected. Teaching and pouring into the next generation has been one of the biggest joys in my life, but recently I have felt stuck when trying to dance personally, unsure of where I belong in it all, or how to simply move for me again.

Being a part of this team in a new way has reminded me why I fell in love with it in the first place. @ohiostatedanceteam continues to inspire me, challenge me, and push me to be better, not just as a dancer, but as a human. I know my journey with dance is changing and evolving, but I’m learning to embrace that change and trust that a new kind of love is still unfolding. I can’t wait to see where it leads 🩷

caption: Happy Birthday, Mom! You’ve been my biggest support through every stage of my life, always standing by me with love, strength, and wisdom. You’ve faced more than your share of hardships, but you’ve always come out even tougher—showing me what real resilience looks like. You’ve never stopped believing in me, especially in basketball, cheering the loudest and lifting me up when I doubted myself. You’re not just beautiful on the outside, but so incredibly smart, thoughtful, and full of heart. You are my world—there’s no one closer to me than you, and no one who understands me like you do. I’m so lucky to have you as my mom. I wish you nothing but happiness and everything you’ve ever dreamed of—you deserve it all. I love you with all my heart💞💞💞 З Днем народження, мамо. Ти завжди була моєю найбільшою підтримкою на кожному етапі мого життя, завжди поруч з любов’ю, силою та мудрістю. Ти пройшла через стільки труднощів, але щоразу ставала ще сильнішою — ти показала мені, що таке справжня стійкість. Ти завжди вірила в мене, особливо в баскетболі, підтримувала найгучніше та підіймала мене, коли я сумнівалася в собі. Ти прекрасна не тільки зовні, але й неймовірно розумна, турботлива та добра всередині. Ти — мій весь світ. Ніхто не є мені ближчим за тебе, і ніхто не знає мене так, як ти. Ти — найкраща людина на цій землі. Я так щаслива, що саме ти моя мама. Бажаю тобі тільки щастя, спокою та здійснення всіх мрій — ти заслуговуєш на все найкраще. Я люблю тебе всім серцем💞💞💞

caption:
Vietnam Day 12: @emk58 & I shared many laughs both together & with our new friends. This trip put in perspective the fact that not everyone has it like most of us do. The orphanages we visited were loving homes to many children across Vietnam. We helped build a home for someone in need. We provided food packages for the poorest communities. We don’t have to walk hours upon hours to get our food. We don’t have to share a room with upwards of 20 kids.  One thing that was very big for me was that inclusion is not recognized as much as it is in the US. Trips like this allow for those children to be seen as the individuals that they are. As opposed to being summed up into a “group”. With that being said, we can always work harder to be more inclusive. 

Please consider donating to @brittanyshope to allow more people to go to places across the world and offer joy & supplies to the people in need. 😊

Thank you to all my friends & family who donated towards this amazing trip 🫶🏼

caption:
Get SHREDDED with these core exercises 💪🏽 

These bodyweight core moves had my abs on 🔥

DETAILS ⬇️

1. Tuck Ups
- bring knees to face, then extend out with control.
- Hits lower abs + teaches compression strength.

2. V-Ups
- Legs + arms straight, meet at the top like a hinge.
- Core killer that builds explosive power + control.

3. Leg Ups
- lay flat, lift legs to 90º 
- Strengthens lower abs + hip flexors big time.

4. Side V-Ups
- Lie on your side, lift legs + torso together.
- Targets obliques for that full core wrap-around 🔁

caption:
What LEVEL are YOU for these body weight exercises?

Tag your level 💪🏽 

BEGINNER – Push-Up Dips
Even hands, lower with control. Great for triceps + chest activation 🔥

ADVANCED – Tuck Planche Push-Ups
Core tight, shoulders protracted, and lean forward! This one teaches control & balance 👊🏽

PRO – Handstand Push-Ups
If you can do a handstand learn this— your shoulders will feel every rep.

GOODLUCK – FULL Extended Handstand Push-Ups
No wall, arms fully extended at the bottom. This is serious strength + control. Only a few can rep this out 🤯
.
.
These progressions helped me LEVEL UP and stay consistent with my upper body goals 💪🏽
Drop your level & your goal for the next one ⬇️

weights are expensive - gravity is free 🚀 

These holds leveled up my core, balance, and body awareness FAST ⚡️

DETAILS ⬇️

L-Hold 
- Core tight, legs straight, chest up. 
- Builds abs, hip flexors & shoulder strength.

Tuck Hold 
- Knees tight to chest, rounded back, arms locked. 
- Great for control + planche prep.

Plank 
- Neutral spine, glutes + core squeezed. 
- Simple but foundational for full-body control.

Tuck Planche 
- Lean forward, hips level with shoulders, full body tension. 
- Major shoulder & wrist strengthener.

Try them out and tag me if you give ‘em a shot 🔁

caption:
I don’t usually post long stuff, but I really want to share the opportunity I got to experience on my trip to Tanzania if you want to read! 

The Hadzabe tribe is the last hunter gatherer tribe in Africa, and one of the last in the world. There are only about 1000 of them left in Africa and they are dwindling fast because they live an extremely hard life. They track no time or age, just day and night. The men spend the entirety of their day hunting for the tribe, and the women gathering other food/supplies. It is common for them to go days without eating, and they pack up and move based on where they are able to hunt best. I was lucky enough to be able to spend a morning with them, since they are hard to find and contact without technology. They also speak a language that is extremely unique and not transcribable since it involves not just letter sounds, but clicks. Regardless, they were beyond welcoming, showed us their homes (there is no home structure, they just sleep on blankets on the ground), and their chief offered to bring us on a hunt with him. In their tribe a chief is based on who is the best hunter. So while he wasn’t very old, he killed a dove with his bow and arrow within 10 minutes of our hunt, made a fire, and then cooked it for us to eat. It was an extraordinary experience that was so eye opening. The average age of death these tribe members (they guess) is around 60, or whenever you are too weak to benefit the group (they leave you to be eaten by hyenas if this is the case). These people will not be around much longer, and if you ever get the chance to visit Africa, I highly highly encourage you to visit them if you can. It will truly change your outlook on life. 

Also included a pic of a leopard at the end which was crazy how much they blend in, but also the chief of this Hadzabe group was attacked by a leopard and ended up winning. An amazing story and he has an insane scar on his neck but I don’t think I got a good picture of it.

caption:
Gave moxa a go to see if it could boost my energy. Moxa is dried mugwort that’s burned over acupuncture points to warm the body and support qi and circulation. Some research suggests it may help with fatigue, but for me this time it didn’t make a difference… on to the next experiment 🤔🤔 

What does the research say about moxa for energy? 👇

doi:10.1177/1550147721991335 : Researchers measured changes in photoplethysmogram (PPG) signals before and after applying moxibustion at acupoints including ST 36, SP 6, and LI 11 over a six-day treatment period. They found that the maximum energy frequency in the PPG increased while the signal amplitude decreased, suggesting that moxibustion may enhance certain aspects of cardiovascular regulation and metabolic activity 

doi: 10.1007/s11655-014-1849-8 although it was a small scaled study only tested on Chinese athletes. The results showed that moxa might be effective for the effectiveness of moxa for exercise. 

https://doi.org/10.1186/s12967-023-04250-z  Relief of Fatigue Using Long-Snake-Like Moxibustion

Another study focused on chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) and compared 30-minute versus 60-minute sessions of a melting-heat technique called “long-snake-like moxibustion.” The 60-minute treatment was significantly more effective at relieving physical fatigue, improving Yang-deficiency symptoms, and increasing thermal radiation in both treated and distant areas, hinting at deeper heat penetration and systemic metabolic warming

#tcm #acupuncture #chinesemedicine #moxa #sportsperformancetraining #running

caption:
Over the past 4.5 years, I’ve been studying and practising Chinese medicine. What started as curiosity has turned into a real passion, and I honestly feel so grateful to be doing this work.

In the clinic, I’ve seen some pretty amazing things happen. From knee pain easing up instantly after just a few needles (and that patient being back playing football in only 3 sessions), to pectoral pain from bench press that had lingered for 3 months disappearing with just ONE needle. I’ve seen people come in with a walking stick and leave without it, patients who were crippled with anxiety find their freedom again, hormones rebalance after pregnancy, and chronic fatigue patients finally get back to enjoying the things they love.

These moments remind me every day how powerful this medicine really is. I never EVER thought I’d finish uni with a 1:1 (I’ve never considered myself very academic), but reading Chinese medicine books and diving deeper into this practice never feels like studying to me….it’s pure joy. Although I was an athlete for over 10 years, I have never worked so hard at something in my life than to get that 1:1. It meant everything to me. 

I feel blessed to have found my passion and purpose outside of being an athlete, and I can’t wait to keep helping more people with this incredible medicine.

Alongside diet I of course prioritised rest and made sure I got a good sleep that night and I honestly have woken up feeling fresh 🙂‍↕️✨🤌. The power of Chinese medicine - it never fails to surprise me❣️

athlete.bio: Hailing from a small town, this tenacious competitor blends finesse with grit. Known for her strategic mindset, she inspires teammates with relentless determination and a contagious passion for the game.

caption:
Pain is a strange thing and we all feel it differently. What might be painful for one person will differ from next whether that be physically or mentally. It so easy to accept that your condition ‘is just the way it is’ and I’m at fault for this too. I once went to a physio and he told me to get into a certain position and I responded by saying ‘I can’t do that, I’ve never been able to do that since my surgery and I’ve been told that is the way it will be forever.’ He told me this was a silly way of thinking and there can always be improvements. He made me step back and think how wrong I was to accept that this was just the way it was. Since that day and with his advice, I started to do more rehab for an old injury and guess what? He was right, it has got better and the things I was never able to do, I now can.

Like I said in this video if acupuncture isn’t for you then please try something else. I am always going promote acupuncture for most conditions because by bringing YOUR body, mind and spirit back into balance you will feel better. I’ve seen people come into my clinic with continuous back pain for 10 years and walk out with no pain.. trapped nerves in the neck causing numbness, tingling, pain and at the end of a series of treatments get better and return to normal. 

Acupuncture is a different way of thinking, it doesn’t use the western approach of treating a symptom. It treats you as a whole. It gets down to the root cause of your problem to remove it, not to mask it. This is honestly why I’m so obsessed with this medicine, it has the power to return you back to YOU with the healing power of your own body. 

#acupuncture #tcm #chinesemedicine #acupunctureedinburgh #pain #surgery

.
.

These past few weeks have been full of ups and downs. After breaking my toe and finding out I would be out for 4-6 weeks, it was a huge toll on me, knowing I would miss BIG’s and potentially be out for the season. Eventually, thanks to time spent in prayer, amazing trainers, strength coaches, dive coaches, and teammates with unconditional support and love, I was able to recover in just 3 weeks—just in time for the meet. Even though there were some things I could’ve done better, it’s always a blessing to represent the Buckeyes. Overall, there were lots of great takeaways. Excited to grow and improve with postseason approaching ⚡︎.

#gobucks!

athlete.bio: A relentless competitor with an insatiable drive, this distance specialist thrives in the heart of the pack. Known for her strategic pacing and infectious enthusiasm, she embodies resilience on and off the course.

caption:
Anyone lucky enough to meet Janet knows how special she was — joyful, silly, and endlessly kind. She was a trailblazer for women's running and will be missed greatly by the running community as well as anyone else who has ever met her.

To me she wasn't just my coach but my biggest supporter. She cared for me as an athlete, but a person even more. Even though she hasn't officially been my coach in 5+ years she was still my first call when I was anxious before a race. Even last year, I was on the phone with her spiraling about racing at B1G's.  The next day she drove over 3h to come to support me while still fighting cancer. 

Anytime I would PR she would also always be my first call. No one was as happy for me as she was.  She helped me overcome injury after injury and setback after setback and never let me quit. This is only a small fraction of the things she has done for me. I am forever grateful for you Janet. I love you to pieces 💛

A special thank you to Mr. Thomas, thank you for believing in me every step of the way and helping me get here.

Congratulations to Nellie Ong who has won the England Girls’ & Women’s Order of Merit titles for 2024.

Nellie qualified 3rd at the French Open to reach the quarter-finals and enjoyed two 2nd-place finishes at the Helen Holm Scottish Women’s Open and the Scottish Girls’ Open, before winning the Welsh Women’s Open Stroke Play Championship.

She also helped England to a bronze medal at the European Ladies’ Team Championship and the Home Internationals as well as the overall gold medal at the Spirit Invitational Amateur Golf Championship. 👏

#RespectInGolf | #TogetherInGolf

caption:
The Buckeye legacy continues ❤️🩶🌰

From baby to now, big girl steps, I’m honored to be a graduate of The Ohio State University as I continue my next walk of life. A 2nd generation alum, both of my parents graduated OSU in the 1990’s. A special shoutout to Papa Fundy as he played basketball along with receiving a degree in Business Finance (Magna Cum Laude), an MBA, and a CFP. Excellence runs in our genetic code! 

To be a Buckeye includes being a part of something bigger than yourself. Every joy obtained, hardship embraced, and lesson learned here at Ohio State is engraved in me as I continue to represent. Thank you to everyone and every experience that shaped me into who I am today. Moments come and go, yet memories last forever. With that said, Go Bucks, both now and forever. O-H…

caption:
Bugün senin doğum günün ama ben içimde öyle bir boşlukla yazıyorum ki bunu… Sanki yıllar geçmiş, sen uzaktasın, ben buradayım, sarılamıyorum sana… Halbuki tek isteğim şu an sana sımsıkı sarılıp içimi dökmekti. Herkes bir gün ablasını sever ama sen benim sadece ablam değil, sanki kalbimin yarısısın. Hani bazen insan yalnız kalır ya kalabalığın içinde, işte sen benim hep o yalnızlığımı gören tek kişiydin.

Beraber büyüdük, beraber güldük, beraber ağladık. Ne zaman düştüysem ilk sen tuttun elimden. Kimse anlamasa da sen hep anladın beni… Ve ben, her geçen gün seni ne kadar çok sevdiğimi daha da fark ediyorum. Bazen uzak kalınca insan bazı şeyleri daha net görüyor. Seni ne kadar özlediğimi, sana ne kadar ihtiyacım olduğunu…

Bugün senin doğum günün ama hediyem yok, elimde bir şey yok… Sadece sana olan sonsuz sevgim ve içimden gelen bu satırlar var. Dilerim bu hayat seni hep hak ettiğin kadar güzel yerlerde tutsun. Senin o tertemiz kalbin, en güzel günleri fazlasıyla hak ediyor.

İyi ki doğdun ablam…
İyi ki varsın…
Ve iyi ki benim en değerlimsin…
Her zaman, her yerde, ne olursa olsun seni çok seviyorum.💜

caption:
Hubo un tiempo en el que tuve que pausar…
Ver desde lejos cómo otros competían mientras yo luchaba con batallas internas que nadie veía.

Sentí que mi talento se apagaba, que las oportunidades se esfumaban…
Pero ahí, justo en medio del desierto, Dios me encontró. 

Hoy, esta medalla no es solo un regreso.
Es una promesa cumplida.
Es la prueba de que la disciplina, la fé y la paciencia SIEMPRE dan fruto.
Es el resultado de muchas lágrimas, muchas oraciones y de no soltarme de la mano de JESÚS, aun cuando no entendía el camino. 

Hoy no solo celebro una medalla.
Celebro a una Natalia que resistió, que confió y que se levantó con propósito.
Toda la gloria, toda la honra, toda la fuerza… al único que lo hace posible: JESÚS. 🙌🏼

Gracias infinitas a mi equipo de México por su apoyo incondicional en cada paso. Esta victoria también es suya. 🇲🇽❤️

caption:
¡Wow! Mi corazón se encuentra en un océano de gratitud hacia Dios por mi tercer lugar en mi primer NCAA. 

Gracias, Don Anthony. Gracias, Dmitri Lapkes. Gracias, Elvis Gregory. Gracias, Iván Trevejo. Gracias, Emily. Gracias, Coach Jack. Y gracias a mi amiga Julieta Toledo por siempre motivarme, darme palabras de aliento y extenderme su mano cuando la necesité.

Desde el día uno en que crucé la puerta de Ohio State, todos mis compañeros me han brindado una hospitalidad tan increíble que no puedo explicar lo feliz y agradecida que estoy por la vida de cada uno de ellos. A mi bello equipo, muchas gracias por esta magnífica temporada, por sus palabras, por sus abrazos y por siempre responderme cuando les doy los buenos días.

A todos ustedes, les doy las gracias por inspirarme este fin de semana a darlo todo. ¡Así de mucho los quiero! :) ❤️

¡Soy orgullosamente una BUCKEYE!

caption: part 2: it’s bittersweet. With today marking my last competition of my senior season, I’m announcing my indefinite retirement from the sport of fencing. This sport has given me so much, and it has also taken an incredible toll on my mental and physical health. I’ve battled chronic pain for the majority of my NCAA career, and it is time for me to take a real, long break from my beloved sport to allow myself to fully heal. I’ve worked hard, on and off the strip, to be here, and I didn’t have any goal other than to be the best teammate and best fencer I can be. I want to particularly express my profound gratitude to Dmitri Lapkes; without his care, wisdom, and guidance, I probably would’ve quit. He believed in me and pushed me the way I needed, and I can’t imagine a better coach to spend four years of early mornings with. I thank my role models who gave me something to strive for, my teammates who challenged and supported me, the athletic trainers who took care of me, and the coaches who paved the way for me to be a D1 collegiate athlete. It’s been a hell of a journey, and now it’s time for something new. But it’s not bye forever—I’ll keep refereeing, and you may see me back in the lamé for vets. But until then: bye for now, fencing. :,)

My growth as a person, and as a leader, is almost entirely due to this beautiful sport challenging me every day to be better. I’ll miss it.

After 14 years of running in circles, it’s time to say goodbye to the track. I’m incredibly grateful for the memories I have created and the lessons I have learned through this sport. I was fortunate enough to have incredible teammates and coaches along the way who never stopped pushing me and believing in me. Bye track, it’s been real😎✌️

caption:
End of an era @ohiostatefencing 

Fenced my last NCAA competition last weekend and ended my collegiate career with a Top 5 finish at NCAA Championships. Feels good to have finished things off on a high note. These past 4 years went by so fast and I wish it wasn’t over yet 😭 It’s been a crazy ride and I can’t say enough thanks to everyone who was a part of my OSU journey. To my women’s foil squad, thanks for being the best squad on the team!! Special shoutout to @elvisgregorygil for everything you do for me, for always believing in me when I didn’t believe in myself, and I couldn’t have done anything without you.

Forever a buckeye ❤️🌰

caption:
I'm still struggling to find the words and process my emotions of it all…

You were more than just another mother to me - you treated me like your own son. Your heart was pure, your soul was precious, and your generosity inspired everyone around you. You had an strong impact on my life, strengthening my faith, love, and confidence. The way you carried yourself and treated everyone reminds me to be a better person every day. I'm forever grateful for the time we shared. You may be gone, but your memory and spirit will continue to guide me. God truly did gain a special angel today✝️. Thank you for being a shining example of love and kindness. I love you forever❤️.

To the Savitt family, especially you J, please know that I'm here for you and love you all. We're a family, and we'll get through this together, just as she'd want us to. We'll stay strong, united, loving, and supported, knowing she's watching over us. 🕊️ #fcancer

Being a first-generation college student, this milestone signifies more than just continuing to play the sport I love. It represents the years of unwavering support of my family.

 Growing up, I often found myself as one of the few Indian players on the field. Despite the rarity of Indian representation in baseball, I embraced my cultural background and used it as a source of strength and motivation.

There aren’t many Indian athletes in baseball, and that’s all the more reason for me to push forward and pave the way for others. I want to show other Indian athletes that they too can achieve their dreams, no matter how unconventional it may seem. 

To all aspiring athletes out there, keep pursuing your dreams. Surround yourself with people who believe in you, and never let go of your passion. Your journey might be different, but it’s those differences that make your story special. Embrace them and keep moving forward.

Go Buckeyes!

4 years went by quick. I am BEYOND grateful and blessed to finish my high school career as a 2x State Champion. People believe I just woke up and became good, which I wish was the case but it isn’t. I have put in countless hours to the wrestling room and trainings with my pops for the longest. I am truly blessed to have my dad who has been in my corner since I have been 4 years old. My mentor, leader, my hero. My mother who spent countless hours making sure I was safe, healthy, and motivated. To my family, I am incredibly grateful for their support, love, encouragement, and sacrifices they’ve made to help me pursue my passion for wrestling. Your belief in me has been my greatest strength, and I am forever grateful to you for your endless support. My senior season was not easy, I wrestled with a lot of injuries that I battled through. However, with the support of my friends and family around me, I was able to overcome the troubles.  Lasty, to @ziggityzow25 , you really stepped up your game this year. You took the bad hand you were dealt with and you overcame the adversity. I love you lil bro. @statechampty2x @keonpricee @loganneff3453 @incrediblekrism @hash7563 @mikeblocher I love yall like my own blood. I will miss my brothas.
ONTO a new journey,  Birdman out. ✌🏽

caption:
I’m done(for now)

Where do I begin with this sport. Wrestling has been my life for the last 15 years. I was just a little kid when I first started and I didn’t know what I was getting myself into. I can’t put words together for the love that I have for this sport. I have so many memories with Wrestling. 

Due to health issues I have decided to take a break away from Wrestling. I don’t know if I’ll ever compete again. This has been an ongoing health issue that many people don’t know about, but truly now I think it’s time to take a break. If this is the end I would like to say thank you to everyone who helped me accomplish everything I got. Personally would thank all coaches that have helped me during these tough times. It has been a long road but Forever Grateful for this journey and the opportunities I have gotten. Thank You Wrestling if this is the end. Go Bucks & God Bless.🙏🏻❤️

caption:
For those who don’t know, I didn’t exactly grow up in Church and knew almost nothing about God before college. I accepted Jesus near the end of my freshman year and began to learn and grow in my faith. I didn’t know what Baptism meant, if I was good enough, or if I was ready. Now I know the point of the Gospel is that we are never good enough and need to be saved by grace through faith in Jesus Christ. Every moment in my life has led to this point and God was with me along the way. I am forever grateful for the blessings, opportunities, and people God has put in my life to learn who he is. 

Today I declared my love, hope, and life to follow Jesus wherever he takes me. God is the only one who truly knows and deeply loves you. I encourage you to find him on your journey in life because you will truly be set free. 🙏✝️ #Jesusislord #Christisking #godisgood #blessed #setfree

caption:
Once you have wrestled in life everything else is easy, that is true for 99% of life but this is tough. A little over a month ago I pictured myself competing in March, not sitting in a recliner all day. It’s humbling to see how vulnerable we can be at our lowest but with the help of God and the people He put in my life we can get through this. 

To get somewhere you have never been you have to do something you have never done. I don’t know what the end looks like but I know that if you keep moving you will come to a better place. I never expected my collegiate career to be plagued with injuries, but I know that God’s plan is better than my own. I am so excited to see what he has set out for me when I return.

caption: Saying goodbye to Columbus has been way harder than I expected. I’m the first to talk shit about Cbus, but I still truly love the place, the people, and change it’s brought me. All the memories, successes, mistakes, and regrets will continue to shape me for a lifetime. I’m grateful for everyone that I’ve met- good, bad, or ugly- and the impact you’ve had on me. Truth is, I still don’t feel ready to move on, but will I ever? I really can’t put into words how much I wish I had more time, but life is moving me on to bigger and better things whether or not I’m ready. That’s all 🫶🏻

caption:
75 Hard.

For the past 75 days I have taken on a lifestyle challenge. Self discipline is one of the hardest things a person can learn and develop especially in this world today. Learning to tell your self no is one of the hardest things to do yet telling other people no is even more difficult. Learning how to say no without feeling guilty because doing something for yourself will allow you to better yourself and help others in the future. Through this past semester I was enrolled in a leadership and character course and one of the biggest lessons it had taught me was about closing your Saying Doing Gap. It’s one thing to say you are going to do something, however actually doing it is another thing and closing that gap can help you achieve anything you set your mind to. One of the other lessons I took away from this process is not everyone will agree or support you, some will even doubt what you can do. One of the readings that really stuck with me was a quote from David Goggins “You will never in life meet a hater doing better than you”. I have often let the opinions of others and what they say to me and about me affect me and how I feel however after doing this I now know that if a person truly tries to do that to someone they have a lot of other issues they need to fix themselves. Which is okay, people are not perfect and we are all trying to find the best ways through life and our own path. Kindness goes a long way and I want to thank a couple people who have really been helpful for me through this time. I want to thank @shealynk_  for putting up with the concoctions I would have her try in the kitchen as well as supporting me through this. As well as my teammates @ryleigh.kathryn and @aidenbrogan for giving great advice and helping me get the challenge started and answer the questions I had.

caption:
LAWST IN THE LANDS YR 333

This year was seriously a treat😋
I could only be in Legend Valley for 36 hours and it was a rollercoaster of a lifetime😂 I got off of the ride with the most peace and confidence I’ve EVER had going back into reality💫
From hosting the @elev808designs meetup, doing a baddie photoshoot with @hcbwyd (men we can be baddies too shout out @kamaruclothing for making me feel like a baddie), creating content (go check elev808’s TikTok!) , AND headbanging with my besties- this Lost Lands was an everlasting gobstopper full of my favorite people and things🤪😤🤭 I am so proud of stepping into my authenticity more and more everyday🥹 Be yourself so that the people looking for you can find you!!!

I could not be who I am without the love, support, respect, and authenticity from this community.
Y’all have my heart 5ever❤️‍🔥

It is an honor to live life at the same time as all of you beautiful people.

Cheers to life!

See ya in the summer festies✨

caption: Happy one year anniversary to my surgically repaired ankle! Special shoutout to all of the trainers and physical therapists that put up with my frustration during rehab.

caption: Deciding to leave Ohio State to go to Tennessee has been the hardest decision I have ever had make in my life. These last two years at Ohio State has been nothing but a dream come true. Although my academic and athletic career hasn’t gone as planned, I wouldn’t trade these two years for anything. I am blessed to have made memories and friends that will last a lifetime. I am proud to have been a Buckeye. Through every football game and basketball game, every Carmen Ohio and Script Ohio, every cheer national championship and football national championship, I’m proud to have been able to represent The Ohio State University. Columbus will always be a home away from home to me, but it’s time I move forward to my next chapter in life. Even though I will be wearing orange and white next year, my heart will forever bleed scarlett and gray. Go Bucks.

4 PRs, 2 Conference wins, 2 State wins, a NBN appearance, a d1 commitment, a school record, and 1 broken pole.

I also want to thank @phillyjumpsclub and @sam.phillyjumps for being the best coaches a vaulter could ask for. It wouldn’t have been possible without your guidance!

Lastly I want to thank my family and friends who helped get me to practice, cheered me on, and always kept me motivated. Especially @fletcher.erin and @rfletcher302 for everything you have done and sacrificed for me.

I am excited to start the next chapter of my track career and am thankful for everyone who made it possible. Big things coming!

caption:
INDEED, THE END AS A FRESHMAN. 

As I wind down this phase of the season, I want to sincerely express my gratitude to God Almighty for seeing me throughout this period as a freshman - a period filled with unimaginable & unexpected life events and also moments to be proud of.

Let me also acknowledge my coaches, trainers & my teammates for their efforts towards me & making sure I am in great shape to represent this program, The Ohio State, in the best way I can. I am looking forward to working with this great team next season. 

To that end, this is where I draw the curtain for my 2025 season and let go of the world championship in Tokyo later in the year. It is a conscious decision I took in order to give myself time to feel, process, and heal from the demise of my beloved parents that occurred earlier this year. 

Moving on to the next, sophomore.

📸@justinv.creative

caption:
ADY WINS HER FIRST STATE TITLE! 🤩🤩

Her 400m time of 55.76 was the fastest indoor time any Ohio athlete has run since 2019! This mark also gives her the following ranks:
- US #9 (class of 2024)
- US #30 (all grades)
- All-time Ohio #9 

Ady has proven herself as one of the best all around sprinters we’ve ever seen! Not only did she win the 400m, but she placed 4th in the 200 (24.98) and 6th in the 60m (7.69)! She’s the only athlete (boy or girl) who scored in all 3 sprint events!

We’re so proud of what you achieved this season, but we ain’t done yet! On to outdoor!! ✌🏾✌🏾🔋

1st world championships✅
1st time representing Guinea🇬🇳✅

To put on this uniform means I am representing more than myself. I represent a country that gave me culture, language, and expression to be myself. This was the biggest stage yet and I am extremely grateful to have been sharing it with the best in the world. 

Despite my feelings about my performance, I walk away as a NR holder. A title I didn’t have coming in. I am learning this sport each and every day. The small wins will add up. It’s not a matter of “if” but “when”. I close out this season healthy and excited for what’s to come. 

Dieu, Merci. ❤️

‎الحمد لله

caption:
Sooo, the half marathon was an absolute fail 🤣. My knee just wasn’t playing ball, and although I could have potentially run it and hoped for the best, sometimes you have to stop and put your health first and it really wasn’t worth the risk.

Maybe I’ll do a half marathon at some point in my life, maybe not we’ll see. But what I really want to do is put this medicine to the test and see how it affects my own performance.

I’ve got four weeks until the 10k in Glasgow, which feels like the perfect window to experiment with different Chinese medicine modalities and find out which ones give me the biggest benefit. I’m not measuring against strict performance markers…this is more about curiosity and fun just exploring what makes me feel and perform my best 🙂‍↔️✨

#chinesemedicine #acupuncture #tcm #sportsperformancetraining #running #edinburghacupuncture

ZAVRŠENA AKCIJA ♥️

Gospođa Nena je patronažna sestra iz Petrinje kojoj smo prošle godine kroz emisiju provjereno poklonili kombi da bi lakše obilazila svojih 16 pacijenata po selima i brinula se za njih…nažalost i Nena sama ima karcinom pluća i vise nije u mogućnosti raditi..iako je imala dozvolu uvijek me tražiti bilo šta te sada nakon godinu dana je pitala nešto za sebe šta znaci da je stvarno došlo do te razine da vise ne može sama,i ne bi trebala biti sama..ne uz sve nas…
Iako je tražila 500 eura samo da plati doprinose idemo joj omoguciti koji mjesec mira..ne zna to,očekuje da joj pomognemo samo sa tim iznosom za doprinose ali nekako vjerujem u sve nas..

caption:
ZAVRŠENA JE AKCIJA!!!

Dobri moji ljudi,uvijek nekako najviše očekujem od akcija kada plaćamo nečije zdravlje,nečiji život…nebrojeno mnogo puta smo ljudima spasili život upravo našom pravovremenom reakcijom i vjerujem u sve nas da možemo to ponoviti i ovaj put..🙏

Posebno jer se radi o samohranoj majci koja ide na terapije već 3 mjeseca upravo radi naših donacija..i sada je došao trenutak za veliku operaciju nakon kojeg će se ova gospođa moći posvetiti svom životu majke bez straha da li će sutra biti i dalje tu,bas kao šta se bojala na početku kada je i došla na naš popis..toliko je bila bez nade da sam je morao uvjeravati da nam prepusti sve da ćemo se mi pobrinuti za nju..danas je to puno drugačija osoba,puna želje za životom jer ste joj vi probudili tu želju..taj san da će biti sve uredu..🙏

Zato idemo nekako pokušati ostvariti i ovo čudo

Ovaj puta se radi o djetetu od 9 mjeseci…koji boluje od akutne limfoblastične leukemije…i potrebna mu je transplatacija matičnih stanica da bi imao šansu za život….

Pa vas molim da je objavite kod sebe na svoj profil,ovaj poziv da se svi dobri ljudi odazovu…

caption:
Comment “EDIDIONG” and we’ll DM you the link to watch‼️

“Grief doesn’t disappear—you just learn to run with it.”

This week on Beyond the Finish Line with Star, Edidiong Udo shares one of the most powerful stories we’ve ever heard.
After losing both parents within six days, Edidiong still showed up for conference, made it to nationals, and fought to keep going when everything inside him wanted to stop.

Now, after undergoing knee surgery and rebuilding his confidence from the ground up, he opens up about grief, mental health, faith, and resilience reminding us that healing isn’t instant, but it’s possible.

This is more than a story of loss.
It’s about faith, fight, and finding purpose again.

🎧 Full episode now streaming on YouTube & Spotify!

caption:
Always the best week with AHIHA! 🤟🏒 in Chicago.  The event is named after @nhlblackhawks legend and Hockey Hall of Fame member #StanMikita as he founded it in 1974. This year I had the opportunity to coach the Beginners and the Women’s Team — such an inspiring group of players. I always leave this week having met incredible people, both on and off the ice. 

#AHIHA (American Hearing Impaired Hockey Association) is a nonprofit organization that provides a week-long hockey camp for deaf and hard-of-hearing players from across the country. It’s more than just hockey — it’s a community that empowers, connects, and uplifts. 

Thank you to everyone who makes this week possible. Already counting down the days until next year! #ASL #AmericanSignLanguage #Deaf #Inclusion #Accessibility #Hockey @NHLUnites @ahihaorg

caption:
grateful is an understatement.
 it was never about the sport, and that’s something that took me losing the sport to figure out. it was never about volleyball itself, but the people and places that volleyball has taken me to. although my athletic career did not unfold the way i dreamed it would, i could not be more grateful for how it turned out. 

every setback, every challenge, every opportunity has led to me finding myself. the past 3 years have been the toughest of my life, and i wouldn’t be who i am today without them. the injuries, the doubt, the long recoveries have taught me so much resilience and perspective. 

two months ago i made the decision to medically retire, a decision that felt impossible and easily the hardest one of my life. even though closing this chapter is the biggest heartbreak i have ever experienced, words will never be enough to express the gratitude i have for this sport. i have met the best people through it, and that will forever be the part that matters most. closing this chapter hurts, but i’m walking away with a full heart 🤍

caption:
Beyond grateful for the opportunity to be a Buckeye. These past four years have taught me so much about myself about who I am, who I want to become, and what it truly means to give everything you have. I’ve met so many incredible people, been surrounded by different personalities and cultures, and gained experiences that will stay with me forever.❤️

To everyone who has been a part of my journey—thank you. Thank you for believing in me, challenging me, supporting me, and pushing me to be great. None of this would have been possible without the people who stood beside me through every high and every low.

Yes, this season didn’t turn out exactly the way I hoped, but I’m still beyond grateful to have been part of this team. We grew together, learned together, and fought together. I love every one of you more than you know, and I wouldn’t trade these moments or these relationships for anything.

I can’t wait to see what’s next. The story isn’t finished just turning the page.❤️

I feel so grateful to have been a part of this tradition and to have shared it with a group of incredible humans and dancers who brought so much joy and heart to every moment. Nobody else could dance for 5 different artists(!!!!) and laugh their way through a two hour tech rehearsal in the rain as gracefully as you all. I’m so inspired by each one of you. A huge thank you to @realshanlew @ginadepool - the best of the best. Thank you for creating such a magical experience filled with so much laughter and trust. Every day felt like a genuine celebration of dance. Pure enjoyment on so many levels; I am so grateful to have been a part of this with you both! Thank you! :) 

And a quick thank you to @msaagency @breezyotoole @itsgtu @jessicahondel for opening this door for me and guiding me toward opportunities that make me fall in love with this art all over again. 🤍 My first job!! I’m over the moon!!

caption:
At CSG, sisterhood is a thread that connects our students and alumnae across generations. That bond was on full display when we welcomed alumna Nyah Funderburke ’21 back to campus.
As part of the Center for Girls' and Young Women’s Leadership Winter Sports Huddle, Nyah shared her athletic expertise with our community, offering valuable insight on building a personal brand, balancing athletics and academics, and embracing the confidence to lead.
Her guidance reinforced what stands at the core of a CSG education: empowering girls to strengthen their voice, develop their leadership, and believe in their limitless potential.
Once a Unicorn, always a Unicorn — and we are grateful for alumnae like Nyah who continue to uplift and inspire the next generation.

caption:
Welcome to JL Management, @Kassidy.Carmichael!  The Ohio State University freshman will be playing both ice hockey and lacrosse as a Buckeye.  

On the ice, Carmichael won the 2024 IIHF U18 World Championship Gold Medal with Team USA, being named “Player of the Game” for the gold medal game, scoring two back-to-back goals in the third period. Playing for NAHA, she won the the 2025 JWHL Championship, was named a JWHL All-Star and 2025 All-JWHL Second Team. 

On the field, Kassidy played for Westford Academy where she accumulated a long list of accolades including 3x All-American, Eastern Mass All-Star 1st Team and 2025 Boston Globe High School Athlete of the Year Finalist.  Amongst other highlights, she scored the game-winning goal with one second left on the clock to send Westford to the Mass State Lacrosse Championship final.

The Westford, Mass native sure has a bright future ahead of her!  Welcome to the #JLMSports fam, Kas!

caption:
Natalia Botello comparte la importancia del Segundo Selectivo Nacional dentro de su calendario competitivo. Este torneo reúne a los mejores tiradores de México, todos presentes y en la pista, buscando su lugar y dando continuidad a un proceso que exige constancia, disciplina y compromiso.

caption: This year made me think about myself more than I did in my entire life. And I am not saying that just because, but I actually saw the world through my eyes and understand who I am a little bit every day. This may not sound how it should, but I don’t want my 2026 to be a good year that brings every great thing in my life; I want it to be real, I want it to be even more me than I have been my whole life, I want to make mistakes and learn from them, I want to be happy with the new people that I call my friends, and I want to cry by myself and not search for someone to tell me the things I want to hear. I want to live my year to find myself, to love myself, and not to force my mind to think that 2026 is going to be a great year because I don’t want it to be. Living abroad taught me how to be mature and how to make decisions without someone lighting my way to the right way. So I am confidently speaking from my experience, which you may not even care about, but I don’t want to wish for things that are going to stay as wishes; I want to accomplish my not very big dreams one by one. :) I want to change my mindset for the better. I want to choose the life I want to have, not wish for it. Overall, 2025 taught me a lot of REAL things that at first I didn’t want to get, but I am thankful to 2025, to the people who were in it, and to the places that I have been to. Mostly thankful for my family, who stayed right beside me for my every decision no matter how hard it was. I couldn’t do it without you, and my only wish is to have you in my life till I die… 💜

caption:
The best weekend of the year is almost here, and there’s something worth remembering.

UDA Nationals is about celebrating every team that has spent months giving everything they have to this moment—early mornings, late nights, injuries, sacrifices, pressure, doubt, and belief. What people see is a two-minute routine. What they don’t see is the countless hours of work, commitment, and heart that led up to it. Every team on that floor earned the right to be there, and every dancer deserves recognition for that alone.

Opinions are inevitable. That comes with being a fan, a judge, or a spectator. But it’s important to remember that these aren’t just teams, they’re people. Dancers who love this art form enough to pour themselves into it. They step onto that floor trying to tell a story, make you feel something, and share something meaningful. 

That matters.

We’re all working toward the same bigger picture: for dance team to be seen, respected, and valued for the athleticism, artistry, discipline, and dedication it demands. That doesn’t happen by tearing each other down. It happens when we support one another and show up as a united community.

The growth of this sport is incredible. The talent, the exposure, the platform. So let’s lean into it. Let’s cheer louder, support harder, and choose respect over negativity.

You don’t have to love every style or agree with every score. But we can celebrate the courage it takes to step on that floor, honor the work behind the scenes, and make dance team known for its passion, unity, and excellence.

So let’s celebrate dance team this weekend. For what it stands for, what it brings, and what it means.

HAPPY SUPERBOWL🤍

athlete.name: Ellie Wagner
athlete.bio: Hailing from a small Ohio town, this fierce competitor combines relentless determination with a strategic mind. Known for exceptional teamwork and unyielding spirit, she leaves her mark on every game.

caption:
Three years ago, I had hip reconstructive surgery and a labrum repair. This changed my relationship with dance in ways I never expected. For a long time, I thought loving dance meant only doing it—training harder, performing, pushing through. When that became too difficult, I felt lost in my body, my confidence, and the space that had always felt like home. I mourned everything I felt I could no longer do or the way I used to be able to do it. There were moments when being in a dance space brought sadness and frustration instead of joy and fulfillment. Admittedly that was incredibly challenging for me. However, I knew I couldn’t let my injury be the end of my love for dance and was determined to find a way forward even if it looked very different. 

Teaching became my way back. It reminded me that dance isn’t only about what your body can execute, but about connection, growth, and impact. Teaching showed me that my value was never tied solely to what I could do physically, but to how I could support and inspire others.

I still have complicated feelings. I still feel fear—of vulnerability, of not being who I used to be. But I’m learning that love doesn’t disappear when things change—it evolves. What once felt like an ending was actually a redirection and new opportunity. 

This year, I’m changing the narrative. I’m choosing to honor what my body can do and to love dance again—not for validation or comparison, but for me. To get out of my head and back into my body.

And if you’re a dancer navigating injury, grief, or uncertainty: don’t give up, know you have more strength! Your love for dance and its impact in your life doesn’t end after an injury. It may change. It may look different. But it can still be yours.

This year is for DANCING🤍

I’m forever grateful for every coach who believed in me, pushed me, and helped shape me into the player and person I am today. And to my teammates, thank you for making every season special. Thank you Ohio State for an unforgettable final season and for allowing me to finish this journey at the highest level. I’m proud of the path I walked and excited for what’s next. I can’t wait to see what the future holds for myself and my family.

Forever grateful. ✌🏽

caption:
one whole year of loving you…

It’s not every day that you meet someone who finds you at your very lowest, chooses to love you, and actively pursues a journey with you… a journey that would entail a season ending injury, a year long recovery, a battle with mental health, the death of a close friend, and all that in between…

But somehow, some way, God knew I needed you. He knew that your presence in my life would be the thing that kept me going and got me through. 

I don’t know that I’ve ever shared our whole story online before… but for those that don’t know, Nick and I saw each other for the first time in the hospital - the day after I had found out my ACL was torn and was meeting with my surgeon. He just happened to be there getting fixed up too :) 

I don’t believe that coincidences exist when God’s involved. Our story is a perfect example of God’s perfect, intentional plan… one that can seem so hard to understand at times. But God can turn even the lowest of times and the hardest of situations into the most beautiful blessings. You are my blessing, Nicholas. 

A minute and a half can’t capture a fraction of the joy, laughs, and experiences we’ve shared this year… thank you for loving me, choosing me, and for choosing US.. each and every day. There’s no one else in this world I’d want to be by my side through it all. Here’s to many more adventures, moments, and memories made together… I love you forever, Nicholas Deane! ❤️❤️❤️

caption:
Welcome to Real 1 Sports, Luciano Pechota.

Proud to officially announce that Luciano Pechota has signed with Real 1 Sports Agency.

Luciano is one of the most accomplished players to come out of Ohio in recent history. A four-year standout at Saint Ignatius High School, he helped lead @sihscleveland C to three consecutive Ohio Division I State Championships, including back-to-back undefeated seasons, and a national championship. Individually, he was recognized at the highest level — a two-time Ohio Mr. Soccer, two-time Gatorade Ohio Player of the Year, two-time United Soccer Coaches All-American, and ultimately the United Soccer Coaches National High School Player of the Year.

He carried that winning pedigree to Ohio State University, where he became a mainstay in the Buckeyes’ midfield from day one. Over four seasons, Luciano earned multiple All-Big Ten honors, was named Big Ten All-Freshman, and helped lead @ohiostatemsoc to a Big Ten Championship and a College Cup / Final Four appearance. 

Pechota was the first player to walk through the door before Real 1 Sports was ever an agency — before there was a name, a structure, or a long-term plan. At the height of COVID, when fields were empty and the world was shut down, he committed to the work. 6am sessions. Masks on. Pitch dark. No guarantees.

What began as individual training became the foundation for the Real 1 training branch [@r1soccer] , years before the agency side existed [@real1sports]. The long-term vision followed — develop the player properly, send them off to compete at the highest level, college programs like Ohio State, and ultimately guide the transition to the professional game.

Seven years later, that vision has come full circle.

Luciano is a proven winner, a leader, and a professional in every sense. Any club fortunate enough to sign him isn’t just adding a footballer — they’re gaining someone who raises standards and elevates the group.

Proud to walk into this next chapter together.
The work continues.

#Real1Sports #WelcomeToTheAgency

Dear High School Diving,
I couldn’t be more happy and grateful for these past four years. The countless memories and friends made, and overall fun on the pool deck has been amazing to say the least! I couldn’t be more grateful for my family, friends, parents, sister, coaches, teammates, doctors, and anyone else who has helped me get this far in my journey. With all that said, I would like to announce that I am officially hanging up the suit when it comes to my jr career. While the diving was beyond fun and I had so many great experiences learning and getting better, the friendships that I made trump that more than anyone could ever imagine. Looking back on my jr career, there were a lot of special diving moments, but what I really remember is all the friends and great memories that I have made. I couldn’t be more excited for the next chapter, and forever, Go Comets❗️❤️. #4peat

caption:
if you were wondering what some behind the scenes of @brentwoodacademydancers first UDA looked like..
 
In all seriousness, getting to watch these girls (& Milo) perform and come together as one was such a gift. In the past few months, getting to spend time with each of them and hear their dreams and testimonies has healed something so deep in me. 

This year has consisted a lot of overcoming my own fears and wrestling with the Lord. Taking a job to coach dance team after saying no to dance for what I thought would be forever was me solely depending on the Lord’s strength. I didn’t feel in the slightest equipped, nor deserving. “Why would He give me dance back after He closed the door?” 

I was talking to a girl I met last night, and she shared how she feels like God has restored her relationship with songwriting after a season when she believed that dream was no longer possible. She said “He had to take it away for me to have eyes to see that this dream was never about me.” He gives us gifts so that we may use them to draw others closer to knowing Him. Dance was never supposed to be about me. But as soon as I gave it to Him, He has blessed it abundantly.

Now - being on the other side has been exciting, humbling, rewarding, and sanctifying all at once. The second I start to believe I can coach these girls on my own strength, I am reminded of my weakness. This role has brought me to prayer more than ever and I am forever grateful for that. 

To every coach, I see you and SO respect you. Especially to my own coaches, thank you for inspiring me and, without even realizing it at the time, planting the seed for my own desire to coach.
To my girls, thank you for bringing so much joy into my life and being the reason this passion of mine has been re-ignited. I couldn’t adore each of you more. 
And lastly, thank you to my actual ride or die - my “Pom Pom” @saralainemcnew . You have been one of the biggest blessings in my life and push me to be better in more ways than you understand. Thank you for allowing me to be a part of such a special family. I can’t wait to (run all around ESPN with no voice) do this all over again!!
